definition_en: very old, from a time thousands of years ago, like ancient Greece
example: The Parthenon is a famous ancient monument in Athens.

definition_en: the line where one country ends and the next one begins
example: Greece shares a northern border with Albania, North Macedonia, and Bulgaria.

definition_en: not afraid of danger or of difficult things
example: The brave firefighter saved the cat from the burning building.

definition_en: a fruit like an orange or a lemon
example: Oranges and lemons are juicy citrus fruits rich in vitamin C.
image_alt: A whole pink grapefruit, with a cut half and a slice
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) with pink flesh, א (Aleph) and raeky, CC BY-SA 2.5, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5
image_credit: א (Aleph) / raeky / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 2.5

definition_en: deep holes under the ground where people dig out coal
example: My grandfather worked underground in the coal mines for twenty years.
image_alt: A large open-pit coal mine with black layers and excavating machines
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Surface coal mine detail, Gillette, Wyoming, Greg Goebel, CC BY-SA 2.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0
image_credit: Greg Goebel / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 2.0
image_file: File:Surface coal mine detail, Gillette, Wyoming.jpg

definition_en: the land next to the sea
example: Odesa is a beautiful port city situated on the coast of the Black Sea.
image_alt: A rocky coast with blue sea water and white waves
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Rocky Coast El Houaria Tunisia, Aymen FANTAR, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
image_credit: Aymen FANTAR / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

definition_en: to be made up of two or more parts
example: The European Union comprises twenty-seven member countries.

definition_en: to join two things together
example: You need a Wi-Fi cable or router to connect your computer to the internet.

definition_en: a soft red-brown metal, used in coins and electric wires
example: Electric cables are usually made of thin copper wires.
image_alt: Three shiny reddish copper wires inside an electric cable
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Electric guide 3×2.5 mm, Petar Milošević, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
image_credit: Petar Milošević / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

definition_en: to make another one that is exactly the same
example: Press Control and C on your keyboard to copy the text into the clipboard.

definition_en: when the ground shakes suddenly and strongly
example: During an earthquake, remember to duck under a sturdy desk.

definition_en: to move like the water in a river
example: The River Dnipro flows smoothly across the country towards the Black Sea.

definition_en: the gold wool of a magic sheep, in the story of Jason and the Argonauts
example: Jason and the Argonauts sailed on the ship Argo to capture the golden fleece.
image_alt: Jason in armor holding the golden fleece, painted by Rubens
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Jason and the Golden Fleece by Peter Paul Rubens, Yair Haklai, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
image_credit: Peter Paul Rubens / Yair Haklai / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0
image_file: File:Jason and the Golden Fleece by Peter Paul Rubens.jpg
image_modified: cropped gilded museum frame, scaled to 768px, converted to webp

definition_en: a tool for careful work, or for making music
example: A microscope is a scientific instrument used in the school science lab.
image_alt: A silver concert flute resting on musical notes on paper
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Flute with musicial notes, Petar Milošević, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
image_credit: Petar Milošević / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

definition_en: a building or place that is easy to know again, and helps you find your way
example: The Eiffel Tower is the most recognizable landmark in Paris.

definition_en: everything you can see when you look across an area of land
example: The green hills and blue lakes create a breathtaking mountain landscape.
image_alt: Rolling green and gold hills in the countryside under a clear sky
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Tuscan Landscape 7, Martin Falbisoner, CC BY-SA 3.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0
image_credit: Martin Falbisoner / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 3.0

definition_en: not very cold and not very hot
example: Mediterranean countries usually enjoy a mild and pleasant winter climate.

definition_en: the smallest piece of water, air or anything else; it is made of atoms
example: A water molecule is composed of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

definition_en: a very high piece of land, much bigger than a hill, like Mount Olympus
example: Mount Olympus is the highest and most majestic mountain in Greece.
image_alt: The high rocky peaks of Mount Olympus under a clear sky
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Hiking on Mount Olympus 54, Anastasiya Lvova, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
image_credit: Anastasiya Lvova / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

definition_en: with people from many different countries and cultures
example: Our multicultural class has pupils from Ukraine, Georgia, Albania, and Greece.

definition_en: something very bad that nature does, like an earthquake or a flood
example: Floods, earthquakes, and forest fires are serious types of natural disaster.

definition_en: a place that makes electricity from the energy inside atoms
example: Ukraine has several nuclear power plants that make electricity.

definition_en: a deep hole that people make in the ground to take out oil
example: Engineers drilled an oil well deep beneath the seabed to extract petroleum.
image_alt: A pumpjack pumping oil in a field under a blue sky
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Gnitz (Usedom), Ölförderpumpe -- 2010 -- 2673, Dietmar Rabich, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
image_credit: Dietmar Rabich / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

definition_en: someone who likes meeting and talking to new people
example: Nikos is an outgoing boy who quickly makes new friends at school.

definition_en: to put text or a picture that you have copied into another place
example: First copy the picture, and then paste it into your presentation slide.

definition_en: land with water on three sides of it, like the Peloponnese
example: The Peloponnese is a famous peninsula connected to mainland Greece by the Isthmus.
image_alt: The Peloponnese peninsula seen from space, surrounded by sea
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, The Peloponnese from ISS, NASA / ISS Expedition 59, Public domain
image_credit: NASA / ISS Expedition 59 / Wikimedia Commons / Public domain

definition_en: a large flat area of land where farmers grow food, like the plain of Thessaly
example: Farmers cultivate wheat and corn across the vast green plain of Thessaly.
image_alt: A wide and flat green plain with farm fields to the horizon
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Plain of Thessaly, Robin Rönnlund, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
image_credit: Robin Rönnlund / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

definition_en: to put words or pictures from a computer onto paper
example: Can you please print three copies of the geography project for our team?

definition_en: a large group of people whose families come from the same part of the world
example: People of every race and background live together peacefully in modern cities.

definition_en: water that flows in a long line across the land to the sea or a lake
example: The River Thames runs straight through the historic heart of London.
image_alt: A river between green fields and trees
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, The Brynica River flowing through meadows on the border of Sosnowiec and Katowice in the morning, Krzysztof Popławski, CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0
image_credit: Krzysztof Popławski / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY 4.0
image_file: File:The Brynica River flowing through meadows on the border of Sosnowiec and Katowice in the morning.jpg

definition_en: to look carefully for something you want to find
example: Pupils use the school tablets to search for information about European geography.

definition_en: to break something into two parts
example: The mighty river flows south, splitting the capital city in two halves.

definition_en: how hot or how cold something is
example: In summer, the afternoon temperature often reaches thirty-five degrees Celsius.

definition_en: under the top of the water, in a sea, a lake or a river
example: Divers discovered an underwater cave filled with colorful sea plants and fish.
image_alt: A fish swimming underwater over the sandy sea floor
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Gallito (Stephanolepis hispidus), franja marina Teno-Rasca, Tenerife, España, 2022-01-06, DD 16, Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
image_credit: Diego Delso / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0
image_file: File:Gallito (Stephanolepis hispidus), franja marina Teno-Rasca, Tenerife, España, 2022-01-06, DD 16.jpg

definition_en: the clean water that comes to the homes in a town or city
example: Lakes and mountain reservoirs protect the city's clean drinking water supplies.
image_alt: Clean drinking water flowing from an outdoor stone fountain tap
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, Benasque - Anciles - Grifo 01, Basotxerri, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
